item.description: Democratic Party of Korea floor leader Han Byung-do said Tuesday that the ruling party will draw up a comprehensive plan to reform the police organization and establish a trustworthy investigation system. Han made the remarks one day after a body believed to be that of missing woman Jang Mi-ran was found on the southern resort island of Jeju following a delayed search caused by a police officer's false closure of her missing-person case. The case drew particular attention as the police are set to assume greater investigative responsibilities in October, when prosecutors will lose their independent and supplementary investigative powers under sweeping prosecution reforms spearheaded by the ruling party. item.title: 'Portrait of a Family' delivers warmth amid dark realities
item.description: Filmmaker Lee Ji-won, who earned critical acclaim with her 2018 movie "Miss Baek," is expanding her thematic scope from isolated individuals to nontraditional family ties in "Portrait of a Family," crafting a story that explores resilience in the face of harsh realities. The film follows baseball star Joong-goo (Ryu Seung-ryong) and high-profile actor Nam-mi (Ha Ji-won), whose lives fall apart when Joong-goo's secret daughter Dong-joo (Kim Si-a) appears. Eight years after their public downfall, the estranged family must reunite, as Dong-joo becomes embroiled in a middle school student's death. While the movie tackles uncomfortable social issues, such as power imbalances and prejudice, its strength lies in its emotional core. Rather than leaving audiences in despair, Lee offers a message of hope and tries to show how broken people can find solace by choosing to stand by one another. Ryu brings deep emotional weight to the lead role. He captures the quiet pain of a fallen star who finds his sole motivation in his drive to protect his daughter. item.description: Foreign tourist arrivals in Korea surpassed 2 million in July, rising more than 20 percent from a year earlier and exceeding pre-pandemic levels, tourism data showed Tuesday. The number of foreign visitors reached 2.09 million last month, up 20.8 percent from 1.73 million a year earlier, according to figures released by the Korea Tourism Organization. The total represents 144.6 percent of the arrivals recorded in July 2019, before the coronavirus pandemic severely disrupted international travel. Chinese tourists made up the largest group with about 777,000 visitors, followed by travelers from Japan at 330,000, Taiwan at 261,000, the United States at 150,000 and Hong Kong at 76,000. Compared with July 2019, arrivals from Taiwan increased by 129.4 percent. From January through July, Korea received 12.8 million foreign visitors, a 21.3 percent increase from the same period last year. China remained the largest source of visitors during the January-July period with 3.99 million arrivals, followed by Japan with 2.28 million, Taiwan with 1.41 million, the United States with 960,000 and Hong Kon

item.title: Coffee franchise Angel in Us to reenter Indonesian market
item.description: Korean coffee franchise Angel in Us, operated by Lotte Group affiliate Lotte GRS, said Tuesday it will reenter the Indonesian market through a master franchise agreement with a local company. Angel in Us signed the agreement with Indonesian food and beverage company Bogajaya Group to open an outlet by the end of this year, the company said in a press release. A master franchise agreement allows a master franchisee not only to open franchise units within a specified area but also to sub-franchise them to third parties. "Lotte directly operated Angel in Us outlets alongside its Lotteria burger chain in Indonesia for several years before withdrawing from the Southeast Asian market in 2020," a company spokesperson said. Through its partnership with Bogajaya, Angel in Us plans to open 10 outlets over the next five years, aiming to establish Indonesia, home to a population of about 270 million, as a strategic base for its global expansion. Lotte GRS currently operates 240 Angel in Us outlets in Korea, with no overseas outlets currently in operation.

item.title: Sejong Institute Korean test expands nationwide as demand grows
item.description: The King Sejong Institute Foundation will administer its 13th Sejong Korean Language Assessment on Sept. 19 at 14 testing centers across seven cities and provinces, expanding access for foreign learners in Korea. Applications opened Monday at 9 a.m. and will remain available through Sept. 6 at 11:59 p.m. through the Sejong Korean Language Assessment website. The foundation introduced the assessment in Korea for the first time this year, after previously administering it only overseas, and the September test will be the second domestic administration following the June session. The number of testing centers has increased to 14 from five, the foundation said, as demand for Korean-language proficiency testing grows among foreign learners living in Korea. The Sejong Korean Language Assessment measures communication skills in four areas: listening, reading, writing and speaking. item.title: Lee says police will be biggest power, stresses need for reform by gov't body
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung said Tuesday the police will soon wield the greatest power among government agencies, calling for the formation of a government body to be in charge of police reform. The president made the remarks at a Cabinet meeting following the recent passage of a revision to the Criminal Procedure Act, which, when enacted, will completely strip the prosecution of all investigative authority, leaving such power solely to the police. They also come after the discovery of the presumed body of a woman reported missing on the southern Jeju Island. A police officer on Jeju reportedly closed the missing person case without confirming her whereabouts or safety, prompting a public outcry over lax police investigations. "As there is skepticism about whether (police) are qualified to exercise their great authority, I hope (the government) will consider how to reform the police, how to establish a (government) body" that will oversee police reform, Lee said. item.title: T'way Air sees 90% international load factor as travelers spread their wings
item.description: T’way Air carried about 3.8 million international passengers in the first half of 2026, as demand for overseas travel pushed its average international load factor to about 90 percent. The airline carried about 5.6 million passengers overall during the six-month period, with international traffic rising about 12 percent from roughly 3.38 million passengers a year earlier. The strongest routes shifted with the seasons, offering a snapshot of how Korean travelers chose destinations throughout the first half of the year. In January, Cheongju-Fukuoka and Daegu-Fukuoka were among the most popular routes, while Cheongju-Osaka and Cheongju-Fukuoka led in February. By March, demand had moved toward resort destinations, with Incheon-Boracay and Incheon-Nha Trang among the top-performing routes. April brought strong demand for Incheon-Bangkok, Incheon-Sapporo and Gimpo-Songshan, while Daegu-Fukuoka led in May and Incheon-Bangkok and Incheon-Sapporo topped the list in June. item.title: CHA Biotech wins government backing to advance cell and gene therapy platform
item.description: CHA Biotech has secured government backing for a three-and-a-half-year research project aimed at pushing its cell and gene therapy platforms toward clinical development, with 31.5 billion won ($22.7 million) in funding. The biotechnology company said Tuesday that it was selected for a follow-up research and development project under the 2026 K-HERO Development and Support Program, led by the Ministry of Science and ICT and administered by the Korea Industrial Technology Association. The program supports corporate research centers working on national strategic technologies, with the goal of developing core technologies and turning them into commercial products. CHA Biotech will use the funding to develop and commercialize two platforms, CHAMS, a standardized source-cell platform based on mesenchymal stem cells, and CHAGE, which uses therapeutic genes to enhance cell function. The company said it plans to combine the platforms into a development system that can be applied across a range of hard-to-treat diseases, rather than being limited to a single condition. item.title: BLACKPINK's Jisoo to release new solo single on Sept. 4
item.description: Jisoo of K-pop girl group BLACKPINK will release a new solo single, titled "Click," on Sept. 4, her agency Blissoo said Tuesday. The release will mark her first new release as a solo artist in 11 months, following "Eyes Closed," a collaborative single with British singer Zayn, formerly of boy group One Direction, in October. Blissoo said further details about the upcoming song will be released later. Jisoo made her debut with BLACKPINK in 2016. She released her first solo EP, "Amortage," in February last year, which topped iTunes' Top Albums charts in 45 countries and regions.

item.title: Supreme Court sides with Trump administration on mail voting restrictions ahead of midterms
item.description: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court opened a path Monday for possible implementation of President Donald Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting, though it remains unclear how much can be put in place before the fast-approaching midterm elections. The decision leaves room for additional court challenges that could further slow Trump's order, and other similar cases have already been filed. The U.S. Postal Service laid out how it would implement the order last week, but time is running short to impose major changes. North Carolina is sending out ballots Sept. 4 overseas and to military voters, and other states will quickly follow suit in just a few weeks. The Supreme Court's conservative majority didn’t decide the legality of Trump's order, instead ruling that states who sued did not have the legal right to challenge it. While the emergency order is not final, it does have the potential to create chaos around voting across the country, with Trump often questioning the integrity of elections and the nation's highest court again the possible arbiter of a political controversy. “

item.title: LX Pantos completes complex defense logistics project for KAI
item.description: LX Pantos, the logistics arm of LX Group, said Tuesday it has successfully completed a complex cross-border defense logistics project involving the transportation of air-to-air missiles from France to Korea for Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI). The project was part of KAI’s development program for the marine attack helicopter, a domestically developed helicopter system for the Republic of Korea Marine Corps led by the Defense Acquisition Program Administration. The missiles, supplied by a European defense contractor, were transported from Chateauroux Airport in France to Incheon International Airport aboard a dedicated charter flight arranged by LX Pantos. They were then transported by road to their final destination at a Marine Corps unit in Pohang. LX Pantos said the missiles were the sole cargo aboard the charter aircraft to meet stringent safety and security requirements. The shipment was classified as Class 1 explosives and was subject to strict security controls as defense material. item.title: EV-related complaints, petitions rise 1.8-fold over 3 yrs
item.description: Electric vehicle (EV)-related complaints filed with the government have nearly doubled over the past three years, the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission said Tuesday. About 173,000 EV-related complaints and petitions were filed with the government's online petition portal and local governments between August 2023 and July this year, with the average monthly complaints rising 1.8-fold to 6,578 cases from 3,683 in 2023, according to the commission. The commission has issued a "complaints advisory," a warning system triggered when petitions in a specific sector rise sharply. Many of the petitions and complaints were about violations of charging area rules and demands for more charging facilities. The commission said it has recommended related agencies strengthen oversight of charging areas, improve maintenance and expand charging infrastructure.

item.title: Hanwha Aerospace to launch US entity for LNG business
item.description: Korean defense firm Hanwha Aerospace said Tuesday it will establish a U.S. entity dedicated to its liquefied natural gas (LNG) business as part of its effort to strengthen its presence in the global energy supply chain. Hanwha Horizon USA will serve as a control tower for the company's LNG operations, overseeing areas ranging from procurement to sales and trading to logistics. Hanwha Shipping CEO James Sagar will also head Hanwha Horizon USA. The U.S. entity will initially secure LNG for Hanwha Energy's LNG power plant in the southern Korean city of Yeosu, scheduled to come online in 2029, the company said. It also plans to supply LNG to other power plant operators and energy companies, and expand into LNG trading across Asia and other global markets. Hanwha Aerospace said the LNG initiative is part of broader efforts to enhance Korea's energy security and strengthen energy cooperation between Korea and the United States. item.title: Ruling party, gov't stress active fiscal policy to boost growth in 2027 budget
item.description: The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) and the government on Tuesday stressed the need for the active role of fiscal policy and investment in future industries, as the government eyes a record-high budget for next year. "Above all, we should focus our fiscal capacity on securing leadership in future industries," DPK floor leader Han Byung-do said during a consultative meeting between party and government officials on next year's budget proposal. He urged the government to set priorities on where and how to allocate the budget, emphasizing the need to strategically invest in areas supporting the youth, region-led growth and future industries. President Lee Jae Myung earlier announced that the government will draw up a record-high budget of around 800 trillion won ($540 billion) for next year and use the additional tax revenue expected from the ongoing semiconductor boom to create the "future response fund" to invest in future industries, policies for young generations and regional development. item.title: Public hearing set for Wed. over integration plan of military academies
item.description: The defense ministry will hold a public hearing this week to collect opinions over its plan to integrate the academies of the three military branches, officials said Tuesday. The public hearing is scheduled to take place at 2 p.m. Wednesday and will include debate between professionals and an inquiry session, according to the ministry. The move comes as the ministry pushes to combine the military academies of the Army, Navy and Air Force into a single institution at Jaundae, a compound of military training and education facilities in the central city of Daejeon. The plan is part of President Lee Jae Myung's election campaign pledge. During the hearing, six participants, including graduates of the military academies and professors, will engage in debate, followed by a Q&A session. The ministry said it will closely monitor various perspectives from the hearing and draw up an optimal plan for the envisioned establishment of the "National Military Academy." item.title: Seoul shares trim losses late Tuesday morning on retail buying
item.description: Seoul shares trimmed earlier losses late Tuesday morning on retail buying as investors awaited major corporate earnings results, including those from U.S. chip giant Nvidia, due this week. After opening 2.4 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) pared losses, trading 117.57 points, or 1.76 percent, lower at 6,579.39 as of 11:20 a.m. Retail investors and institutions bought a net 1 trillion won ($723 million) and 503 billion won, respectively, while foreigners sold a net 2.11 trillion won. The index fell more than 3 percent the previous session on a sharp decline in chipmakers, such as Samsung Electronics, amid renewed concerns over the profitability of artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments. Overnight, U.S. stocks closed mixed, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 0.26 percent, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 0.76 percent. Investors are also weighing escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East while awaiting U.S. economic data and corporate earnings due this week, analysts said. Federal Reserve Gov. item.title: Korea to develop environmental, ocean observation satellite
item.description: Korea will develop a next-generation environmental and ocean observation satellite by 2033 to succeed the current geostationary satellite, the country's space agency said Tuesday. The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA) said the proposal to develop the Cheollian-6 satellite has passed a preliminary feasibility review for a state-funded research and development project. The proposed satellite is scheduled for launch in 2033, with an estimated budget of about 770 billion won ($556.7 million). It will take over the observation missions of Cheollian 2B, which was launched in 2020. Cheollian-6 will be tasked with monitoring the environment and oceans, enabling authorities to more quickly detect and track air and marine pollution as well as maritime disasters. The geostationary satellite will be developed using homegrown technologies, including a hybrid propulsion system. It will also be equipped with instruments capable of simultaneously conducting both environmental and ocean observations from a fixed position relative to the Earth, according to KASA.

item.title: Hyundai Motor, labor union tentatively reach wage deal
item.description: The management and labor union of Hyundai Motor Co. tentatively reached a wage agreement early Tuesday following a series of strikes that caused production disruptions. The two sides reached an understanding at the 17th round of talks, agreeing to raise monthly base pay by 100,000 won ($72.20), provide a performance bonus of more than 400 percent of monthly salary and pay an additional payment of 12.5 million won, the automaker said in a release. The two sides also agreed to extend the retirement age from the current 60 to 65 if related laws and regulations are revised. If the agreement is approved in a union vote scheduled for Aug. 31, this year's wage negotiations at South Korea's largest automaker will be concluded. The 400,000-member union staged a combined 60 hours of strikes this year, resulting in about 120 hours of production disruptions across two shifts. The labor action included a full-day strike Friday, the union's first such walkout in 10 years. The strikes are estimated to have caused cumulative production losses of around 55,200 vehicles, with lost sales exceeding 2.3 trill

item.title: BOK faces rate dilemma amid stronger growth, record household debt
item.description: The Bank of Korea (BOK) faces a dilemma over whether to raise its policy rate at a meeting later this week, as stronger-than-expected economic growth supports another hike while record-high household debt poses a growing concern, market watchers said Monday. The central bank will hold its Monetary Policy Board meeting Thursday to decide the policy rate, which currently stands at 2.75 percent after the BOK raised it by 25 basis points last month. Markets are closely watching whether the central bank will deliver a second consecutive rate hike or pause after last month's increase. Economists who expect another rate hike point to stronger-than-expected second-quarter growth and continued inflationary pressures. Korea's economy grew 0.6 percent in the second quarter from the previous quarter, supported by strong semiconductor exports. Park Jeong-woo, an economist at Nomura Securities, said the growth momentum remained strong. item.title: How Daejeon evolved from 'boring city' to 'city of bread'
item.description: In 2019, Daejeon Metropolitan City made an unusual pitch to tourists, asking them to post their own flowchart for visits to what it jokingly called “Boring Daejeon.” It worked like a decision tree for visitors to Daejeon. Participants could answer “yes” or “no” to questions about the city and where to go, but no matter the path, it always ended the same way: “Stop by Sungsimdang — a historic bakery nestled in the heart of Daejeon.” The humorous chart reflected how Daejeon is widely seen even by its own residents as a dull and uninteresting city, a place without the standout attractions that drew people to other comparably-sized cities. Despite this reputation, last year the city drew 90.94 million visitors — the most since the Korea Tourism Data Lab began tracking the figures. Nearly half of those visits, 48.1 percent, were driven by food tourism. Much of Daejeon's draw is its bakery scene, led by Sungsimdang, a famed purveyor of bread with a legacy that traces back decades and highlights the city's history as a hub for flour-based foods. item.title: 'No Permission to Dance': Venue closure in Busan leads to petition to change laws on live performances
item.description: Korea may seem to the outsider like a land of K-pop idols and dancing, but the truth is different for those who live here. Due to restrictions, people in Korea have to be careful about where they dance, because if they bust a move in a cafe, bar, restaurant or live music venue, they could get it shut down. The latest victim of this "K-Footloose" regulation is Ovantgarde, a music venue and pub in the southeastern city of Busan. The venue was shut down after municipal authorities visited earlier this month to respond to an unrelated complaint. Although the complaint turned out to be nothing, the officials observed a band performing in front of an audience, and reported the venue for allowing "dancing," in violation of the rules governing its restaurant license. One of the owners of Ovantgarde disputed the officials' claim that patrons were dancing, calling it an "interpretation" and saying instead that audience members were merely "standing and naturally engaging with the performance." The venue was ordered to suspend its business for two months as a first-offense punishment. This is not th

item.title: Trump approval at record low as support for Iran war falls: Reuters/Ipsos
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. public approval of the war with Iran fell to its lowest level since the conflict's early days, helping to hold President Donald Trump's popularity at a record low, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on Monday. The four-day poll showed just 31 percent of Americans support U.S. military action against Iran, down from 37 percent in a March Reuters/Ipsos poll and 34 percent earlier this month. The decline was driven by fewer self-identified Republicans backing the conflict. Some 69 percent of Republican respondents support the war, compared with 77 percent in March. The war has been dragging on Trump's public standing this year, and for the second survey in a row just 33 percent of respondents said they approved of the Republican's performance in the White House, the lowest level in polls from Trump's first or second term. Some 83 percent of the country thinks the war will go on "for an extended period of time," the Reuters/Ipsos poll found, up from 80 percent earlier this month. item.title: US Treasury chief vows to cut every 'economic lifeline' of Iran
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday laid out plans for the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran, expanding Washington's secondary sanctions threats and warning of dire consequences for countries that decline to join the pressure campaign. Bessent's address comes almost six months into a war on Tehran that has ground to a stalemate, with stalled peace talks and Iran preventing most traffic through the crucial Strait of Hormuz. "Around the globe, our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone," Bessent told a press conference. item.title: Trump says to double tariffs on Canada autos as trade fight heats up
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday that he would double tariffs on Canadian vehicles beginning next year, as the neighboring countries spiral towards an escalating trade war. "On January First, 2027, Tariffs on all Cars, Trucks, both large and small, Automotive Parts, and Steel, will be increased to 50 percent," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. The current U.S. tariff impacting Canadian autos stands at 25 percent for non-U.S. content, while imported steel to the United States generally faces a 50-percent duty. U.S. automakers did not immediately respond to queries on the matter. Trump's latest threat comes after the North American neighbors failed Friday to reach a deal to avert new 50-percent U.S. tariffs on select Canadian goods. The duties took effect on Saturday. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has since announced retaliatory tariffs targeting the United States after walking away from what he called a "bad deal." item.title: S. Korea, US diplomats stress 'close' communication on NK, peninsula peace
item.description: SEOUL/WASHINGTON — The top diplomats of South Korea and the United States have agreed to continue "close" communication and cooperation to address North Korea's nuclear issue and promote peace on the Korean Peninsula during a call, Seoul's foreign ministry said Tuesday. Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio held phone talks on Monday (Seoul time), as U.S. President Donald Trump recently declined to answer a question about whether his goal in reengaging with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un is denuclearization, spawning concerns that the United States could acknowledge the North as a nuclear-armed state. In a press release on their talks, the ministry did not mention whether the chief diplomats reaffirmed their commitment to North Korea's denuclearization despite the two sides' emphasis on the importance of cooperation on North Korea's nuclear quandary. item.description: U.S. threats to impose "the toughest sanctions in history" to force Iran to buckle to its demands after nearly six months of war have raised the prospect of a new round of escalation in the Gulf. How could Iran respond to the economic pressure? Can Iran stop more oil getting out of the Middle East? Mohsen Rezaei, the former Revolutionary Guards chief and secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, has already threatened to shut down oil exports — one of Tehran's main strategic approaches since the war began on February 28. item.title: US proposes upping H-1B visa fee to more than $100,000
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration on Monday released a proposed regulation to codify an unprecedented more than $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers that Trump first imposed last year but has been blocked by the courts. The fee first imposed by Trump in a temporary proclamation last year vastly raises the cost of the visas that are heavily relied on in the tech, education and research sectors. A federal judge in June ruled that the fee was illegal and blocked the Trump administration from collecting it. A Boston-based appeals court is reviewing that decision while a different court considers whether a judge in Washington, D.C., properly rejected a challenge to the fee by a major business group. Trump's 2025 proclamation imposing the fee expires in September, one year after it was issued, but directed the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to adopt regulations making it permanent. item.title: Before taking away children's smartphones
item.description: Korea is moving to keep minors off social media and phones out of classrooms, but the adults writing those rules cannot look up from their own screens. A few days ago, heading home from work, I was standing seven stories underground at Daegok Station on Subway Line 3. Six elevators connect to the transfer platform, and long lines backed up at each. I picked the shorter one and waited. The elevator stayed on the second floor. Wrong line? Then I looked at the call button. Dark. Nobody had pressed it. Nobody waiting seemed to have noticed, or cared. Every person in that line was looking down at a phone. I stepped forward and pressed it myself. When the doors finally opened, the commuters filed in with blank faces, eyes still down. "Smombie" is a portmanteau of "smartphone" and "zombie," a term for people who walk without looking up. When the word arrived more than a decade ago, it was treated as a new phenomenon of the smartphone age, something to study. Now it is unremarkable. Anyone can be a smombie a dozen times before lunch, as those commuters were. We have given up the idle minutes betw

item.title: Meet Prairieland Protester Autumn Hill: How Her "Act of Solidarity" Became a 50-Year Prison Sentence
item.source:markdown:
“I’m absolutely being imprisoned for a political agenda,” activist Autumn Hill tells _Democracy Now!_ in a phone call from Texas’s Johnson County Correctional Facility, where the 30-year-old trans woman is serving a 50-year prison sentence for protesting outside the Prairieland ICE jail last July. Hill is one of nine protesters convicted of terrorism-related charges after federal prosecutors accused them of being members of an “antifa terror cell.”
In an interview with _Rolling Stone_ writer Jack Crosbie, Hill says that she had no intention of committing violence at the protest, which ended when a police officer was shot and wounded by a fellow protester who says he fired in self-defense. No other injuries were reported, and Hill says she had already left when the shooting occurred. “It was my belief that we would go home at the end of the night to continue eating and drinking and be merry. We truly didn’t think that anything was going to go wrong. And we didn’t expect or want any violence to occur.”
For prosecutors pushing the overly broad and poorly substantiated idea that anti-fascist organizing against the Trump administration is violent and dangerous, the Prairieland case was a “gold mine,” says Crosbie. “There’s no real burden of proof. They can just say that you’re 'antifa,' and that becomes sort of gospel, according to the government.”
item.author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)

item.title: Illinois Is a Sanctuary State, But Cops & Prosecutors Still Secretly Work with ICE: Injustice Watch
item.description: We speak to journalist Aura Bogado, whose new investigation into Illinois law enforcement and prosecutorial collaboration with ICE has revealed that dozens of immigrants have been arrested and deported with the help of local officials in violation of the state’s sanctuary law. “Those are 150 individuals whose lives were very often changed, communities completely split apart,” says Bogado about her reporting. She further explains that while “there are constitutional rights for everybody, that [are] afforded to every person, … those rights are suspended in the immigration context. The bar that is needed to prove a case for deportability is so much lower.”

item.title: U.S. Threatens New Economic War on Iran by Targeting China & Tehran's Other Top Trading Partners
item.description: The Trump administration has announced unspecified plans to further tighten sanctions on Iran, threatening other countries, including China, in the process. We speak to sanctions expert Nicholas Mulder about what he calls the “rhetorical” and “psychological warfare” of the announcement. For Iran, says Mulder, the announcement was not “really materially all that meaningful. And to the extent that they are, they hurt ordinary Iranians and not the government.” The impact on the U.S. relationship with China, however, could be much greater. If the U.S. does place secondary sanctions on Iran’s trading partners, the “U.S.-China trade truce might be unraveling,” warns Mulder. “The space for maneuver that the U.S. has in using these tools of very coercive economic statecraft has narrowed.”

If the U.S. does place secondary sanctions on Iran’s trading partners, the “U.S.-China trade truce might be unraveling,” warns Mulder. “The space for maneuver that the U.S. has in using these tools of very coercive economic statecraft has narrowed.”

item.title: Roseline Hamel and Nassera Kermiche: Beyond sorrow
item.description:
On the sidelines of the 2026 Rimini Meeting for Friendship Among Peoples, Roseline Hamel and Nassera Kermiche, who have come to be known as “sisters in sorrow", speak to Vatican News about the tragedy that unites them. Roseline is the sister of Fr Jacques Hamel, the French priest who was killed while celebrating Mass in a terrorist attack in 2016. Nassera is the mother of one of the two teenagers who perpetrated the attack and was subsequently shot dead by police.

item.title: China's Xi likely to visit India with big delegation for 1st time in 7 years
item.description: NEW DELHI — Chinese President Xi Jinping is likely to attend next month's BRICS summit in New Delhi with a large delegation, three sources said, in what would be his first visit in seven years and a fresh sign of a thaw between the rivals. India is hosting the September 12 to 13 summit, where Xi's presence would be watched less for the BRICS agenda than for what it signals about Beijing and New Delhi's efforts to stabilise relations after deadly border clashes in 2020. "Chinese officials are busy finalising hotels and security protocols," one of the Indian sources with direct knowledge told Reuters. Last year, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited China for the first time in seven years, but the relationship has only improved gradually. More recently, a fresh border-related dispute triggered sharp diplomatic exchanges between the two sides. Two other Indian sources said Xi was likely to be accompanied by a delegation of about 400 officials, compared with fewer than 200 officials the last time in 2019. Officials from both countries are expected to use the summit to explore ways to

item.title: Nvidia worker among 9 charged in Taiwan chip smuggling case
item.description: TAIPEI — Nine people in Taiwan, including a Nvidia worker, were charged on Monday over the illegal export of artificial intelligence servers to China, Taiwanese prosecutors said. The indictments follow an investigation into the shipment of "high-end" AI servers made by Nasdaq-listed Super Micro Computer and containing advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls. Eight of the nine defendants were charged with breach of trust and forging documents to smuggle 74 servers containing Nvidia chips to China, Keelung District Prosecutors Office said in a statement. Of those servers, 50 were transhipped through Indonesia, eight were sent via Japan and the rest were exported directly to China. An additional 56 servers were seized at Taiwan's border, the statement said. Three of the defendants have been charged with embezzlement. The United States restricts exports to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips used to power artificial intelligence systems, designed by industry leader Nvidia. But it is not a criminal offence in Taiwan — a situation lawmakers and experts sa

item.title: Ukraine wants peace but won't give in, Zelenskyy says on Independence Day
item.description: KYIV — Ukraine wants peace but will not just surrender to Russia at any price, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a defiant speech on Monday to mark Independence Day, as foreign leaders pledged their support. Flanked by British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Council President Antonio Costa, Zelenskyy praised the resilience of the Ukrainian people during more than four years of war with Russia. "Ukraine absolutely wants peace, but it is not ready to simply surrender," Zelenskyy said, warning that Russia would not halt its aggression even if Ukraine ceded to its demands for more territory in the country's east. Wearing a traditional Ukrainian embroidered shirt, Zelenskyy thanked several foreign leaders for travelling to Kyiv to show their continued backing, on the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's break from the Soviet Union. Burnham, who took office last month, said his choice of Kyiv for his first foreign visit showed the importance he attached to assisting in Ukraine's defense. item.title: Attacks on Red Cross in DR Congo making Ebola fight 'harder'
item.description: GENEVA — The Red Cross on Monday voiced alarm after six workers taking part in a desperate bid to contain a deadly Ebola outbreak were injured in attacks last week in the Democratic Republic of Congo. "Attacks against volunteers and humanitarian personnel are unacceptable," the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement said in a statement, along with the Red Cross societies of the DR Congo and Uganda. The statement said that on August 17, a Ugandan Red Cross convoy helping the Ebola response was attacked in Ituri province — the outbreak's epicentre — with one person seriously injured, and two ambulances pelted with stones and vandalised. The following day, two volunteers were injured while attempting to conduct a burial in Haut-Uele province. They were evacuated for medical care, during which two vehicles were damaged. Then on Wednesday, in Beni, North Kivu province, three volunteers were "attacked and injured", with equipment used in the Ebola response destroyed. The statement said the attacks were an alarming reminder of the risks faced by humanitarians when tackling epide

item.title: France readies high school phone ban from new term
item.description: PARIS — The French government said Monday it would press ahead with a ban on mobile phones in high schools from the start of the new school year. In July, France's parliament approved legislation banning both social media access for children under 15 and mobile phone use in high schools. But earlier this month, the country's top court struck down the social media provision, dealing a blow to President Emmanuel Macron, who had championed the measure. However, the Constitutional Council did not rule on the separate provision banning mobile phone use in high schools. On Monday, government spokesperson Maud Bregeon said Macron "has decided to promulgate the law" containing the ban on phones, despite the Constitutional Council striking down its flagship provision, a ban on social media for under-15s. "As a result, the ban on mobile phones in high schools can take effect from the start of the new school year, with a stable, consolidated and statutory legal framework," she told reporters after a cabinet meeting. item.description: TOKYO (AP) — A cross-party group of Japanese lawmakers headed to Beijing on Monday seeking to mend strained ties following Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s comment on Taiwan that angered China and led to tensions that have spilled over into the economy. The group, which includes Gaku Hashimoto, a lawmaker of Takaichi's governing Liberal Democratic Party and a former health and welfare vice minister, and a lawmaker each from the Komeito and Centrist Reform Alliance opposition parties, will meet with Chinese Communist Party officials during a visit through Thursday. “Communication has been severed in all areas and we are beginning to see their impact in many areas,” Shinichi Isa, a spokesperson for the CRA party, told reporters before leaving Tokyo's Haneda airport. “I hope we can somehow find a clue to restart a dialogue.” Soon after taking office, Takaichi said a Chinese attack on Taiwan could constitute “a survival-threatening situation” for Japan that would justify the use of force, enraging Beijing. item.title: 4th missing person found dead on Jeju over 3-day span
item.description: A body believed to be that of a man in his 70s was found in waters near eastern Jeju Island on Sunday, the Jeju Coast Guard said Monday. The Coast Guard said the man had been reported missing Saturday and is investigating the exact cause of his death. The body was one of four believed to be those of missing persons found on Jeju Island over the past three days, including that of Jang Mi-ran, a 37-year-old woman who had been missing since May. Earlier on Monday, another missing person was found dead near a valley on the west side of the island. On Saturday, a man in his 60s was found dead in the northeastern part of the island. Police had been looking for the man after the police officer in charge of Jang's case had prematurely closed the case, prompting his family members to report him missing again last week.

item.title: Lee likely to meet Samsung chief for possible discussion on chip projects: sources
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung is likely to meet with Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong this week to possibly discuss the country's three mega projects centered on semiconductors and artificial intelligence (AI), sources said Monday. The meeting came days after President Lee met with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won. Lee is also likely to have a meeting with Hyundai Motor Group Executive Chair Euisun Chung this week, the sources said. The talks came amid speculation the United States is demanding South Korean investment in its semiconductor industry as part of Seoul's investment commitment to the country, although Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said earlier that no related talks had been held with Washington.

item.title: Pakistan's Munir spoke to Trump ahead of Tehran visit, sources say
item.description: ISLAMABAD — Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir spoke with U.S. President Donald Trump last week, according to three Pakistani sources, days before Munir was expected to hold talks in the Iranian capital of Tehran on Monday. The call, which has not been previously reported, came as the U.S. threatened to roll out major economic sanctions targeting Iran and its trade partners. The White House Office of the Press Secretary did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It was unclear what Munir and Trump discussed.

item.title: Court grants bail for power broker in 'free opinion poll' case
item.description: An appellate court on Monday granted bail for a jailed self-proclaimed power broker convicted for providing free opinion polls to former President Yoon Suk Yeol between 2021 and 2022, legal sources said. The Seoul High Court accepted Myung Tae-kyun's request for bail, about a month after a lower court sentenced him to an 18-month prison term on charges of violating the Political Funds Act. The lower court found Myung guilty of making illegal political contributions by offering the opinion polls for free to Yoon and his wife between June 2021 and March 2022. The district court sentenced Yoon to a two-year prison term in the case. With the Seoul High Court's decision to grant bail, Myung will stand his trial at the appellate court without physical detention.

item.title: Is my kimchi safe? China formaldehyde cabbage scandal puts Korea on alert
item.description: Chinese authorities have launched a nationwide food safety inspection after cabbage sellers in northern China were found using formaldehyde solution to keep the vegetables fresh, prompting Korea to strengthen inspections of Chinese cabbage imports. Formaldehyde is classified as a Group 1 carcinogen. China's State Administration for Market Regulation said Sunday that it had instructed local authorities to investigate and swiftly address the use of formaldehyde solution in Kangbao County, Zhangjiakou, Hebei Province, according to China's state-run Xinhua News Agency on Monday. The administration, together with the Food Safety Office of the State Council and the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, also ordered authorities to trace the distribution routes of the affected cabbage and prevent it from entering the market. Authorities were also instructed to conduct special sampling inspections and market checks nationwide targeting cabbage and other vegetables prone to spoilage. The case came to light after an account on Douyin, China's version of TikTok, posted a video filmed at a cabbag

item.title: Lee nominates special inspector to investigate corruption involving president's family, close aides
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung has nominated a former prosecutor as the special inspector in charge of investigating corruption allegations involving the president's family and key aides, a presidential spokesperson said Monday. Presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung announced the nomination of Choi Kil-su, a former senior prosecutor, from among three candidates recommended by the rival parties and the bar association. Kang initially said Lee has appointed Choi as special inspector, but Choi is required to undergo a confirmation hearing at the National Assembly before his appointment. If appointed, Choi will become the first special inspector to serve in the position in a decade. The independent inspector general position was established in 2014 under then President Park Geun-hye, but it has been left vacant since 2016. By law, the National Assembly must recommend three candidates with at least 15 years of legal experience, from which the president is required to select one. item.title: Korea's AI ethics principles lack binding force, specificity
item.description: The government's new artificial intelligence (AI) ethics principles provide a broad framework for responsible AI use but lack legal force and specific implementation standards, experts noted, raising questions about their practical impact. The government announced national principles for the ethical development and use of AI on Monday, setting out three core values and seven guidelines for AI use across industries and everyday life. The principles provide a common but nonbinding reference for developers, providers, users, government agencies and civil society, the Ministry of Science and ICT said. Choi Kyoung-jin, director of the Center for AI, Data and Policy at Gachon University, said the principles should be viewed as a broad declaration of values rather than a set of enforceable rules, with their effectiveness ultimately depending on how they are translated into sector-specific practices. “The principles should be understood as declaring the fundamental principles that we need to think about in this era,” Choi said. “Ethical principles are something that would be good to follow

item.title: Lee administration sidelines Seoul mayor in housing push
item.description: The government and ruling party are drawing speculation that they are sidelining Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon in their push to expand housing supply. Housing demand is most concentrated in the nation’s capital due to the heavy concentration of population, jobs and urban conveniences, making the Seoul mayor a key local government partner in the central government's bid to address housing supply. But Cheong Wa Dae, the Cabinet and the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) appear to be finding ways to bypass Oh rather than consulting him on housing supply policies for Seoul. item.title: Lee accepts justice minister's resignation: presidential spokesperson
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung has accepted Justice Minister Jung Sung-ho's resignation, a presidential spokesperson said Monday, a week after the minister offered to step down. "President Lee accepted Minister Jung Sung-ho's resignation, as he expressed difficulty in continuing to carry out his duties due to deteriorating health," presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung said. The government plans to appoint Jung's successor promptly to avoid any disruption to state administration, Kang added. Jung submitted his resignation last week, citing the completed legislation of a prosecution reform bill, as well as health issues. Under the legislation, prosecutors will be completely stripped of their investigative authority, leaving investigative powers entirely in the hands of the police. With Jung's departure, two ministerial seats are now vacant, including the post of minister for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which was vacated by Prime Minister Han Seong-sook.

A day after Kim made his first official public appearance since suspending his activities, his agency, Gold Medalist, shared two photos on its official social media account Monday. The photos show Kim surrounded by flowers and gifts apparently sent by fans during his visit to Indonesia. In one, he smiles while holding a large bouquet, while in another, he flashes a victory sign toward the camera. The agency's post followed Kim's appearance Sunday as a special guest on Indonesian broadcaster RCTI's 37th anniversary live show, "Mahakarya RCTI 37." Videos shared through RCTI's official account show Kim smiling and greeting a large crowd of local fans who had gathered to see him. item.description: The ruling party and government have agreed to ease the simultaneous increase in property holding and capital gains taxes for non-resident single-home owners, party officials said Monday. The agreement puts the government’s real estate tax reform package, unveiled on Aug. 3, back under review just three weeks after its announcement. “The government will broaden the circumstances under which periods of nonresidency can be recognized as residence when justified, while listening to public concerns and seeking a more reasonable solution,” Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol said during his appearance before the National Assembly. The reconsideration comes amid growing resistance within the ruling party and mounting public complaints over housing policies, particularly in Seoul. item.title: Oman top diplomat to visit Iran to discuss Hormuz Strait
item.description: TEHRAN — Oman's foreign minister will travel to Iran on Tuesday, Iran's foreign ministry said, as Tehran and Muscat seek a way to regulate the passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz. Badr al-Busaidi will hold the "ongoing political consultations between the two sides, as two littoral states of the Strait of Hormuz, to help strengthen peace and security in the region," Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in a statement on Monday. "The visit is aimed at strengthening Iran-Oman bilateral cooperation and al-Busaidi will meet with Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to discuss bilateral and regional issues," Baqaei added. Iran has exerted control over Hormuz, a key waterway for oil and gas shipping, since the outbreak of the war in the Middle East on February 28. It requires vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the waterway. item.title: KOSPI plunges more than 3% as Samsung, SK hynix shares tumble
item.description: The KOSPI fell more than 3 percent Monday as weakness in Samsung Electronics and SK hynix weighed on the broader market, reversing gains posted over the previous two sessions on expectations that the two semiconductor heavyweights would boost shareholder returns. The benchmark index opened 31.88 points, or 0.46 percent, lower at 6,881.07 before extending its losses to close at 6,696.96, down 215.99 points, or 3.12 percent. Foreign investors led the selling, offloading a net 3.69 trillion won ($2.67 billion) worth of KOSPI shares, while institutional investors sold 1.29 trillion won. Retail investors bucked the trend with net purchases of 3.32 trillion won, cushioning the market’s losses. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix shares dropped 8.70 percent and 3.41 percent, respectively, with the disparity in their losses largely attributed to differences in the shareholder return measures announced last week. item.title: Author Jo Jung-rae returns with love story, calls literature defense of humanity
item.description: Novelist Jo Jung-rae, best known for sweeping epics chronicling Korea’s modern history, has returned to romantic love in his new two-volume novel, “Seorikkot,” (frost flower in Korean). He said that literature must preserve human imagination and feeling in an age increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence (AI) and smartphones. At a press conference in Seoul, the 83-year-old author said his new work, which may be his final full-length novel, was the first work in his 56-year literary career with love at its center. “I wanted to write a sad love story,” Jo said. “But this is not a simple love story.” The novel marks a notable departure for Jo, whose landmark historical trilogy — “Taebaek Mountain Range” (1989), “Arirang” (1994) and “Hangang” (2001) — has long been regarded as one of Korean literature’s most ambitious attempts to narrate the country’s 20th century upheavals. item.description: A top presidential aide said Monday that the chief justice's recommendation of Supreme Court justice nominees without prior consultation may have infringed on the president's authority to appoint public officials. Hong Ik-pyo, presidential secretary for political affairs, made the remarks during a parliamentary session, a week after Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae recommended two sitting regional court judges for appointment as new Supreme Court justices by the president. Cho, appointed by former conservative President Yoon Suk Yeol, made the recommendations in writing, without following the customary practice of making recommendations to the president in person after prior consultation on the nominees. Cho, appointed by former conservative President Yoon Suk Yeol, made the recommendations in writing, without following the customary practice of making recommendations to the president in person after prior consultation on the nominees. "I share the view that the president's appointment authority has been infringed on to a certain extent," the presidential secretary said after being asked about the issue by Rep. item.title: 'You can't remove heart from body': FSS, KDIC unions rally against relocation out of Seoul
item.description: “The Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation (KDIC) and the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) are the heart of Korea’s financial stability. And yet the government says it wants to move that heart away from the center of the financial markets. If you take out the heart and put it somewhere else, can you really expect the body to keep functioning normally?” The voice of Kim Young-heon, head of the KDIC labor union, rang out under the sweltering sun outside Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul, Monday. “Heart transplant surgery is among the most delicate procedures, where even a single mistake can be fatal. Keep in mind that our financial system has no anesthesia and no recovery room.” More than 40 union members from the KDIC and FSS waved bright red placards as Kim continued his speech at a rare joint press conference protesting a government plan to relocate the institutions to Sejong, Korea’s administrative capital. The relocation drive is part of the Lee Jae Myung administration’s push to move government agencies out of the Seoul area, thus easing the heavy concentration around the capital

item.title: From Tufts art student to Miss Korea: Woo Seo-yoon takes 2026 crown
item.description: Woo Seo-yoon, the daughter of a former national basketball player, has been crowned Miss Korea 2026, with the 22-year-old Tufts University student setting her sights on a career as a global art curator. Woo won the top title of "Jin" at the 70th Miss Korea pageant held at the Coex Auditorium in Gangnam District, southern Seoul, on Saturday. Woo turned emotional as her name was announced, after which she thanked those who had supported her throughout the competition. "I was able to come this far thanks to the support of so many people," she said. "Even people who have never met me supported me online and showed me so much interest. I believe that helped lead to today's result. I am sincerely grateful." Woo also said she understood the responsibility that came with the crown. "I know the responsibility that comes with the crown I received today, and I want to become someone who has a positive influence on society," she said. item.title: IBK under scrutiny over internal controls after major fraud case at China unit
item.description: The Industrial Bank of Korea (IBK) is facing scrutiny over its internal controls after its Chinese subsidiary lost 83.4 billion won ($60.3 million) due to financial fraud that allegedly went undetected for months. According to documents submitted Monday by IBK and the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) to Rep. Shin Dong-wook of the People Power Party, IBK's Chinese subsidiary provided non-face-to-face loans to local borrowers in partnership with a non-bank financial institution. The financial institution used an online lending platform to recruit borrowers and collect loan repayments. Borrowers sent their repayments to an account designated by the platform, which was supposed to transfer the money to IBK. However, the platform allegedly changed the repayment account without authorization and diverted the money instead of sending it to IBK. It also allegedly falsified records to make it appear that borrowers had repaid their loans. As a result, some borrowers were marked as delinquent even after making their payments, while IBK failed to receive the money. The incident started in December

item.title: Illinois declares 'BTS Day' ahead of Chicago concerts
item.description: The U.S. state of Illinois has designated the dates of K-pop supergroup BTS' upcoming Chicago concerts as "BTS Day in Illinois," the group's agency said Monday. Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker proclaimed Aug. 27 and 28 (U.S. time) as "BTS Day in Illinois," coinciding with BTS' performances at Soldier Field in Chicago on its "Arirang" world tour. "BTS has transcended international borders and utilizes their platform to champion social causes, including mental health awareness, self-love, and global philanthropy," Pritzker said in an official proclamation. This core messaging of BTS "heavily aligns with the civic values of Illinois, inspiring millions of individuals worldwide — collectively known as the BTS ARMY — to engage in grassroots community service and match global charitable giving." The governor also encouraged local residents to embrace "the unifying values of music, culture and community advocacy." item.title: Seoul opens 40-year-sealed subway passage as K-culture venue
item.description: Commuters passed above it for decades without knowing what lay beneath. Now, a 335-meter underground passage in the heart of Seoul has taken on a new identity. Closed to the public for more than four decades, the tunnel connecting Euljiro 1-ga and City Hall stations on Seoul Metro Line 2 officially reopened Monday as K-Culture Station, launching with “COSMOS,” an immersive exhibition marking the 20th anniversary of K-pop group BIGBANG. Inside the darkened space, large digital screens display colorful digital portraits of the members, while bright yellow crowns — a symbol long associated with BIGBANG — glow across the black floor. The exhibition reimagines the group's two-decade history through light, video and sound across 11 experience zones featuring media art, projection mapping, holograms and interactive displays. “For more than 40 years, a 335-meter underground space lay closed beneath City Hall Station, one of the city’s busiest transit hubs,” Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon said, after passing through digital screens, music and mirrored installations at the K-Culture Station

item.title: Last maternity ward in Miryang closes, forcing pregnant women to travel elsewhere to give birth
item.description: The last remaining maternity hospital in Miryang, South Gyeongsang Province, is set to close next month after 40 years of serving the local community, raising concerns that the collapse of regional maternity care could further accelerate the decline of the nation’s provincial areas. Annual deliveries in Miryang plunge from 400 to 100 Opened in 1986, Miryang Jeil Hospital has been one of the largest hospitals in the region, with 79 beds and departments of obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics and internal medicine. It has handled more than 20,000 deliveries since it opened. In recent years, however, the medical staff operating the hospital’s delivery unit dwindled to just two doctors: the hospital’s director, who is in his 70s, and an obstetrician in his 60s. When the obstetrician announced his intention to leave the hospital, the director decided he had no choice but to close the hospital. item.title: Renault Korea focuses on consistent after-sales service nationwide
item.description: Renault Korea is strengthening its after-sales service network to provide customers with consistent maintenance quality and convenience regardless of where they live or travel in the country. For drivers who plan to keep their vehicles for years, reliable after-sales service can be just as important as the quality of the vehicle itself. If maintenance quality or customer service varies from one service center to another, it can undermine trust in the brand. Renault Korea operates 365 service centers nationwide to ensure customers can easily access maintenance services across the country. The company also provides technical training and standardized maintenance procedures to maintain consistent service quality. One of its key programs is the R:assure Premium Care Solution. item.title: Korea emerges as global test bed for chauffeur-driven luxury mobility
item.description: Korea is emerging as a key test bed for the global chauffeur-driven luxury vehicle market, as Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Genesis prepare to go head-to-head with flagship models targeting corporate executives and business owners. The competition is set to intensify in the second half of this year with the launch of the Genesis GV90, the latest Mercedes-Benz S-Class and BMW's 7 Series. The luxury lineup reflects a major shift in Korea's automotive market where demand for high-end vehicles is expanding beyond mainstream and entry-level segments to some of the world's most expensive cars. Genesis unveiled the GV90, its first ultra-large flagship electrified SUV, in San Francisco on Wednesday, with a Korean launch scheduled possibly around the fourth quarter. The luxury automaker under Hyundai Motor Group is positioning the model's four-seat Neolun Executive Suite as a direct challenger in the chauffeur-driven market, traditionally dominated by large luxury sedans. The top-end GV90 features a wood floor, radiant heating system, refrigerator and table, while the front seats can electrically swivel

item.title: Korea expands autonomous driving AI tests
item.description: The government said Monday it will significantly expand pilot projects for locally developed autonomous driving artificial intelligence (AI) and strengthen support for deep-tech startups as it seeks to accelerate the commercialization of emerging technologies. According to the Ministry of Science and ICT, the government approved measures to accelerate the commercialization of autonomous driving AI and support deep-tech startups during a meeting chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Science and ICT Minister Bae Kyung-hoon. Under the autonomous driving road map, the government will expand pilot projects that began in Gwangju to more regions and larger-scale operations. item.title: Korea opens faster access to NATO standards for defense exporters
item.description: Korea’s arms procurement agency has established its first formal procedure for domestic defense companies to obtain NATO standards, a move aimed at helping them compete for contracts and joint development projects in NATO markets. Until now, exporters had no formal domestic channel for obtaining many of the standards and often had to seek help from local companies or government agencies in countries where they were pursuing business. Under the new system, standards that the Korean government can access directly through NATO’s online database could be provided in as little as a week. The Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) said Monday it has enacted guidelines governing how NATO standards are requested, provided and handled. NATO standards set common requirements designed to ensure interoperability among allied weapons systems, ammunition and other military supplies. They cover areas ranging from protection requirements and testing procedures to communications protocols, logistics and security rules. item.title: Hanmi Pharm signs $2.3 bil. licensing deal with Roche's Genentech for obesity drug candidate
item.description: Hanmi Pharm, a Korean pharmaceutical company, said Monday it has signed a 3.2 trillion-won ($2.3 billion) licensing deal with Genentech, a U.S.-based member of the Roche Group, for an obesity drug candidate designed to reduce body fat while preserving and increasing muscle mass. Hanmi Pharm has signed an exclusive licensing agreement with Genentech for the development, manufacturing and commercialization of its novel metabolic treatment candidate HM17321, a long-acting uro-cortin-2 (UCN2) analog, for obesity and related conditions, including type 2 diabetes, the company said in a press release. Under the agreement, Genentech will have exclusive rights to research, develop, manufacture and commercialize HM17321 worldwide except in Korea. Hanmi will retain the rights to the drug candidate in Korea, it said. "By licensing this next-generation investigational therapy with first-in-class potential from Hanmi, Roche and Genentech will pursue a differentiated approach to selectively reduce fat mass while improving both muscle mass and muscle function," Boris L. Zaitra, head of Roche Corporate

item.title: Disabled activists end subway protests after compromise with DPK
item.description: A disability rights advocacy group announced Monday it would completely halt its subway-riding protests, which have been frequently staged in Seoul to call for increased government spending for people with disabilities and their mobility rights. The announcement from the Solidarity Against Disability Discrimination (SADD) came after the group met with the ruling party members of the Seoul Metropolitan Council and the ruling Democratic Party of Korea's (DPK) Seoul city chapter to declare a "grand social compromise" aimed at guaranteeing the rights of people with disabilities. The participants in the meeting said in a resolution, "We resolve to stand in solidarity until the end to create an equal society where disability is not a barrier and a city where people can enjoy dignity beyond mere survival." The DPK also promised to pass two new ordinances meant to guarantee the mobility and labor rights of people with disabilities at the upcoming plenary session of the Seoul city council. item.title: N. Korea, Belarus near visa-waiver agreement for ordinary citizens: report
item.description: North Korea and Belarus are close to signing a visa-waiver agreement for ordinary citizens, Belarus' state media has reported. The report by the Belarusian news agency BelTA on Sunday (Belarus time) said Belarusian Foreign Minister Maxim Ryzhenkov discussed ways to enhance mutual times with his North Korean counterpart, Choe Son-hui, including the pending deal. "We will sign it in the very near future," Ryzhenkov was quoted as saying. "We discussed the entire range of bilateral relations, including the upcoming contacts through the foreign ministries and the signing of a number of agreements, including this important agreement on visa-free travel for citizens." The report said only "some technical details" were left to be work out. The move is believed to be a follow-up to the March summit in Pyongyang between Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, where they signed an agreement on friendship and cooperation. item.title: US cancels joint marine drills with South Korea over Iran war-related force constraints
item.description: The United States cancelled a joint amphibious landing drill scheduled for next month with South Korea, Seoul's Marine Corps said on Monday, after Washington cited constraints on the availability of U.S. forces due to the war in Iran. The U.S. Marine Corps formally notified its South Korean counterpart in June that force availability would be constrained for the division-level exercise, known as Ssangyong, a South Korean Marine Corps spokesperson told a press briefing. The allies remain in close consultations on resuming the drills, the spokesperson said. He did not specify what measures might be taken to prevent future cancellations or to make up for lost training opportunities. U.S. Forces Korea did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The cancellation follows U.S. President Donald Trump's surprise order to scale back a separate annual joint military exercise that ended last Friday, citing the cost and Seoul's refusal to take part in the Iran war. Trump also wrote on his Truth Social platform that the Ulchi Freedom Shield drills sent "a signal that was totally inappropriate

item.title: Samsung forecast to overtake Apple in global smartphone shipments in 2026: report
item.description: Samsung Electronics is forecast to reclaim the top spot in the global smartphone market this year, overtaking U.S. rival Apple, an industry report showed Monday. Samsung's smartphone shipments are expected to rise about 0.8 percent from a year earlier, according to Counterpoint Research. Apple's shipments are expected to decline 2.1 percent this year. Samsung's relatively strong performance is attributed to its broad product portfolio, geographically diversified business presence, in-house component sourcing capabilities, and robust carrier and distribution networks, which have helped strengthen its competitiveness amid supply chain uncertainties, the report said. On the other hand, Apple is facing potential price hikes for the iPhone 18 series phones as well as changes in the launch schedules for individual models. In addition, Apple is only expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone in the third quarter of this year, with initial shipments projected to be only a few million units, making it unlikely to significantly alter the overall shipment trends in 2026, the latest findings said.

item.title: NCT 127 feels like it's starting over on 10th-anniversary album
item.description: NCT 127 releases its seventh full-length album "BLINGY" on Monday, opening a new chapter in its 10th anniversary year with three of its original members absent. The Seoul-based unit of SM Entertainment's sprawling NCT roster debuted in July 2016 with the stated ambition of taking the city to stages worldwide. Hits including "Cherry Bomb," "Kick It," "Sticker," "Fact Check" and "Walk" have kept the group in the sights of global fans over the past decade. The team is now operating as a five-member act made up of Taeyong, Johnny, Jaehyun, Yuta and Haechan. Vocalists Doyoung and Jungwoo are fulfilling their mandatory military service, while Mark left the group in April after his exclusive contract with SM ended. Hours before the album's release, the five members held a press conference Monday at Lotte World Tower in Seoul's Songpa District, where they spoke about the comeback and their 10th year in the industry. item.title: Illegal imports of obesity drugs surge 3.5-fold in Korea
item.description: The number of illegally imported obesity treatment drugs detected surged in the first half of this year, driven largely by drugs ordered from foreign websites and shipped through international mail. According to the Korea Customs Service (KCS) Monday, authorities detected 4,155 instances of illegal imports of Mounjaro, Wegovy and other obesity drugs between January and June, nearly 3.5 times the 1,189 cases for all of last year. Novo Nordisk's Wegovy and Eli Lilly's Mounjaro are both once-weekly injectable obesity treatments that suppress appetite. Wegovy launched in Korea in 2024, while Mounjaro followed in 2025. Illegal import cases have risen quickly since the two drugs' domestic debuts, from four cases in 2024 to 1,189 last year and more than 4,000 in the first half of this year. By comparison, only 596 cases were formally cleared through customs via import companies over the same period, rising from 14 in 2024 to 191 in 2025 and 391 in the first half of this year. item.title: Foreign students in Korea call for support after graduation
item.description: With more than 320,000 foreign nationals now studying in Korea, international students say the hardest part may begin when university support ends: finding jobs, changing visas and securing housing on their own. The Korea Times held a discussion, Thursday, with five students from Iran, China, Russia, India and the Philippines to hear about their experiences and discuss ways to improve support after graduation. The students said government and university programs often focus on life during enrollment, leaving graduates to navigate the transition into employment and longer-term residency with limited practical assistance. Ghazal Esmaeili, an Iranian master's student at Korea University who has spent three years in Korea as a Global Korea Scholarship recipient, said she had rarely worried about visa or daily-life issues because of scholarship and university support. But she said the end of that support would leave her responsible for finding a new visa status and employment, making the transition daunting. item.title: Appeals court upholds 18-month prison term for ex-presidential aide over martial law document
item.description: An appellate court on Monday upheld an 18-month prison term for a former presidential secretary for drafting a false document linked to former President Yoon Suk Yeol's failed martial law bid. The Seoul High Court upheld the lower court's ruling that found Kang Eui-gu guilty on charges of creating a false official document by drafting a cover of Yoon's martial law proclamation, three days after his declaration on Dec. 3, 2024. The appellate court ruled that Kang had drafted the document and collected the signatures of Yoon, then Prime Minister Han Duck-soo and then Defense Minister Kim Yong-hyun, to give Yoon's proclamation an appearance of procedural legitimacy. "The defendant was aware that the date of signing by Yoon Suk Yeol and others differed from the actual date the document was drafted," the court said. A special counsel team indicted Kang over the martial law document in December. He was immediately taken into custody and imprisoned after the lower court ruling in May.

item.title: Samsung SDS to build AI-ready network for Seoul National University
item.description: Seoul National University is preparing to overhaul its campus network in a project designed to support large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) research and move the university toward an AI-native campus. Samsung SDS said it won the project to transform the university’s network platform, covering 243 buildings and serving about 50,000 students, faculty members and staff. The new infrastructure will provide network speeds of up to 800 gigabits per second, allowing large volumes of data used in AI research and education to move more quickly across the campus. The project will also introduce logical network segmentation to strengthen security and network automation to improve operational efficiency. For students, the upgraded system is intended to provide more stable connectivity in classrooms, laboratories and libraries while reducing slowdowns and interruptions. Researchers and professors will be able to transfer large AI training and research datasets more reliably over the higher-bandwidth network, the company said. item.title: US vows 'economic D-Day' as Iran threatens to halt all oil exports
item.description: CAIRO/WASHINGTON — The U.S. threatened Iran with what it called "the greatest financial offensive ever marshalled" as it prepared to roll out economic sanctions on Monday that target Iran's trade partners. Iran in turn vowed to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf "if the economic war continues." U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will hold a press conference at 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT) on Monday amid promises to reveal even more severe measures on a country that has endured near-continuous economic sanctions since the Islamic Revolution of 1979. "At dawn begins an economic D-Day — the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary," Bessent wrote in an opinion piece published in the Financial Times on Sunday. The warring nations have not conducted military strikes against each other for weeks, but they also have not engaged in meaningful talks to end the six-month-old conflict. The telecommunications company said Monday that it is expanding its IT modernization efforts under a strategy called Next IT, with AI and automation to be incorporated across development and operations. item.description: Fadu is betting that the next wave of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers will reshape the role of flash memory, unveiling a broader technology portfolio as it seeks to expand beyond its traditional focus on solid state drive (SSD) controllers. The data center semiconductor company said Monday that it presented its AI data center strategy at the 2026 OCP Korea Tech Day held Friday at COEX in Seoul. The annual conference, organized by the Open Compute Project Foundation and the OCP Korea community, drew about 1,500 attendees this year, bringing together hyperscalers, semiconductor companies, infrastructure providers and startups. During a keynote address, Fadu researcher Kim Seung-min discussed how the explosive growth of data in AI data centers is changing requirements for flash memory, SSDs and controllers. Kim said the rising volume of data and the cost of processing it are emerging as critical challenges for AI infrastructure. item.title: EcoPro BM begins overhaul of Hungary plant to target European EV market
item.description: EcoPro BM has begun converting its Hungary plant to produce high-nickel cathode materials for European premium electric vehicles (EVs), as the battery materials maker moves to deepen its foothold with global automakers. The company said Monday that it is modifying an existing nickel-cobalt-aluminum (NCA) production line at the plant to also manufacture nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) materials, with shipments to European customers expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027. The conversion is expected to require about 40 billion won ($29 million), according to the company. EcoPro BM outlined its European business plans at an investor briefing at NH Investment & Securities’ headquarters in Seoul on Friday, saying it had begun investing in the plant’s conversion to supply high-nickel cathode materials to a German premium automaker. The Debrecen plant, which began commercial operations in the first half of this year, has an annual production capacity of 54,000 tons and currently operates NCA lines.
